title: 單輪23億，累計43億，無問芯穹重新整理國產AI Infra賽道融資雙重紀錄
abstract: 單輪23億，累計43億，無問芯穹重新整理國產AI Infra賽道融資雙重紀錄 克雷西 2026-10-13 12:01:15 來源： 量子位 算力、模型、行業，三層生意一起做 克雷西 發自 凹非寺 量子位 | 公眾號 QbitAI 23億元，AI原生基礎設施服務商無問芯穹已完成C輪融資。加上前幾輪，無問芯穹累計融了43億元，單輪和累計都創下了國產AI原生基礎設施賽道的新紀錄。 無問芯穹自成立以來投資方陣容匯聚多方知名機構，涵蓋國資機構、產業投資方、財務投資機構等多個類別。其中，國資機構包括杭州高新金投、社保中關村基金（君聯資本管理）、珠海科技產業集團、廈門國興投資、徐匯資本、孚騰資本、中保投資、國開科創等；產業投資方包括Dabanc Holding、聯想、九坤創投、同歌創投、騰訊、百度等；財務投資機構則包括紅杉中國、洪泰基金、惠遠資本、啟明創投、達晨財智、順為資本、礪思資本等知名機構。無問芯穹已成為AI Infra賽道最受追捧的明星獨角獸之一。 這家公司不訓模型、不做應用，它做的是模型和晶片中間那一層，具體來說是把模型和晶片連起來，實現多種模型演算法與多種晶片硬體間的極致效率與成本最佳化。 這樣做的目標，是高效聚合協同異質、碎片、跨域的算力資源，從每一度電、每一秒晶片運轉中，「榨」出低成本、高質量、生產級可用的Token，並推動Token進入真實業務場景。 在海外，市場已經給這門生意標好了價格。做同一門生意的三家公司，過去一年估值全部搭上了火箭。 Fireworks AI從40億美元漲到175億美元，漲了337%；Baseten漲了160%；Together AI漲了151%。 這三家背後，還站著同一個我們再熟悉不過的投資人。 輝達。 靠著賣鏟子在GPU產業鏈最上游賺得盆滿缽滿的輝達，親自下場押注下游的AI Infra，生怕錯過AI Infra需求大爆發時代的船票。 賣鏟子的都急了，說明這塊市場的潛在空間已經大到讓上游坐不住了。 輝達在賭的事情，無問芯穹的投資人顯然也想賭。這輪23億砸進來，押的就是這塊市場。 算力缺口，是個無底洞 理解這筆融資的背景，要先看一個事實。 你以為晶片變強、產能提升，AI算力的缺口就會彌合，但實際上算力從來沒有夠用的那天，因為晶片產能再怎麼擴張，也追不上需求的增長。 因此，獨立研究分析機構SemiAnalysis創始人Dylan Patel判斷，算力短缺會一直持續。 而Agent的爆發，又把這個缺口放大了一個數量級。 一個Agent跑一次任務，背後是幾十個推理請求連環呼叫，Token消耗量跟過去的單輪對話完全不可同日而語。 資本的嗅覺非常靈敏，很快就帶著資金殺了進來。 開頭提到的三家海外AI基礎設施公司，走勢已經很能說明問題，整個AI Infra賽道都在被重新定價。 20VC創始人Harry Stebbings聊起對Fireworks AI的投資，說「15分鐘就敲定了，是十年投資生涯裡最容易的決定之一」。 15分鐘，一個管了十年基金的人，只用了不到一頓飯的時間，就投了一家AI Infra公司。 在Agent的催化加速下，算力的缺口非但不會被填上，反而只會越撕越大，這筆生意也就望不到天花板。 同一條賽道，海外已經跑出百億美元估值的公司，而在國內，也剛剛誕生了這條賽道融資額的新紀錄。 而且無問芯穹這家公司沒有選擇自己建機房，走了一條不同的路。 不建機房，也能做AI Infra 做AI Infra，其實不外乎兩條路。 比較傳統的做法是自建機房，拿重資產換規模，但這極有可能意味著要揹債擴張。 另一條則走向了另一端，機房壓根兒不碰，把散落在各處的算力收集起來，靠軟體編排把它們織成一張網。 無問芯穹選的就是後者。它自身並不擁有實體資料中心，算力資源散佈在各地的算力中心，晶片的廠商更是「萬國造」。 無問芯穹的技術體系有三個關鍵詞，多元異構、軟硬協同、自主式AI。 先說多元異構，無問芯穹的平臺已經適配了輝達、AMD、華為昇騰、壁仞、海光、摩爾線程、沐曦、燧原科技、平頭哥等16種晶片，服務著37000P算力。 哪怕新來一款晶片，團隊也只用2個工作日就能適配完，國產晶片的適配成本砍掉了70%以上。 如今晶片供應鏈越來越複雜，能在不同晶片之間自如切換，客戶不用綁定在一款晶片上，這個能力可謂是相當硬核。不僅是不綁定，無問芯穹還保持中立，作為連線模型、晶片和客戶需求的獨立平臺，將分散的模型能力和異構算力組織起來，持續最佳化從底層資源到AI生產力的轉化效率。 無問芯穹率先做到了千卡規模的異構晶片混合訓練，算力利用率達到97.6%。更具體一點，無問芯穹運用了華為昇騰、天數智芯、沐曦、摩爾線程四種國產晶片與AMD、NVIDIA兩種進口晶片，完成了700億參數大模型異構晶片混合訓練。這在行業裡是頭一個。 跨域訓練也是一個硬指標。 無問芯穹聯合中國電信完成了國內首例超4000公里的大模型跨域混訓，把新疆哈密和廣東深圳的算力拉通，在300億參數模型上做聯合訓練，效能提升了165%。 除此之外，團隊還打通了4個不同代際、不同型號GPU叢集的多資料中心聯合訓練，以及本地私有叢集和公有雲算力的混合雲混訓，效能分別提升41%和68%。 當然了，適配只是其中一步，實際執行起來，速度也是一項重要指標。 畢竟Agent可沒時間等著模型一個字一個字地往外蹦。 這就是軟硬協同要解決的問題。 無問芯穹在軟體棧上做了一整套最佳化，從自動化並行編排與搜尋、運算元及計算圖最佳化，到計算與通訊重疊、動態編排與排程，將計算資源高效轉化為高質量的模型效能與Token服務能力。 最終的結果是，在無問芯穹最佳化後的基礎設施上，萬億參數MoE模型的訓練吞吐比主流開源框架高了41%到75%。 推理這邊，無問芯穹通過一系列技術創新，一年內把推理成本降到了原來的十分之一。 2026年WAIC上，公司又釋出了業內首創的跨叢集異構PD分離架構PDD（Prefill-RelayDecode-MainDecode），首Token延遲降低51.5%，單Token成本降低37.5%。 隨著PDD的規模化應用，未來推理成本還有十倍的下降空間。 但Agent時代還有一個問題，模型擅長的能力並不相同，所以具體任務該調哪個模型、用多少算力就成了需要操心的事。 無問芯穹把這道判斷題交給了系統，也就是他們所說的「自主式AI」。 具體來說，引入大小模型的自適應協同機制，系統把複雜任務交給大模型做規劃和推理，輕量級的即時響應則丟給小模型，系統根據任務複雜度、時延要求和Token成本動態切換。 在這套機制之上，無問芯穹還部署了一組智慧體蜂群，目前已包含三個子集：面向使用者的平臺管家智慧體系統、面向叢集的運維智慧體系統，以及面向晶片的運算元生成智慧體系統。通過Agent能力驅動整套AI Infra形成自主迭代、自我最佳化的閉環，讓基礎設施越用越強。 把這些能力放在一起看，無問芯穹做的事情就很好理解了。 他們立足基礎設施，向下匯聚能源和晶片，向上支撐模型和應用，不僅極致提升底層資源向AI生產力轉化的規模和效率，更有著Agentic AI時代最顯著的AI原生能力——用基礎設施智慧體蜂群賦能資源規模擴展、提效Token生產，並支援Agentic AI的持續進化，具備業務前瞻性。 算力、模型、行業，三層生意一起做 技術這邊的賬算完了，再看商業化。 無問芯穹提出了「前店後廠一中心」的戰略佈局，具體來說就是把業務拆成三層。 最底下一層是算力集散中心（Agentic Infra自主式基礎設施平臺），乾的活就是把散落的、異構的算力資源統一匯聚、彈性排程、按需分發，為模型與應用層築牢充足、穩定、可擴展的算力底座，客戶不用操心底層硬體差異，接進來就能用。 中間一層是Token工廠（Agentic MaaS大模型服務平臺），用極致效率服務Token的規模化、高質量生產。目前該平臺已經和智譜、月之暗面等頭部大模型公司達成密切合作，上線了百餘款大模型，客戶不用自己部署，選好模型就能開箱即用。 最上面一層是AI生產力商店（行業解決方案），面向企業提供Agentic Infra行業解決方案。對於同一個行業場景，不同模型規模和不同硬體配置可能對應完全不同的Token成本，無問芯穹以智慧體場景自適應技術作為提升AI生產力轉化效率的核心技術路徑，已推出覆蓋文娛遊戲、醫療健康、法律服務、能源電力等領域的Agentic Infra行業解決方案，使Token進一步轉化為可執行、可交付的行業生產力。 Agent應用爆發後，無問芯穹大模型服務平臺日均Token使用量半年漲了超過40倍，95%以上的推理任務都來自Agent。 無問芯穹三層業務裡，算力集散中心為模型與應用層築牢充足、穩定、可擴展的算力底座；Token工廠通過一系列原始技術創新，極大提升大模型推理效率，降低推理成本；AI生產力商店則把Token高效轉化為產業認可的高質量AI生產力。 早在2025年，無問芯穹就在業內率先提出了Agentic Infra的範式變革。如今，Agentic Infra支撐智慧體規模化執行與持續進化的產業價值正在被不斷驗證。等風真的來的時候，它已經站在了風口上。 23億砸下去，賭的是什麼？ 技術跑通了，需求也驗證了，接下來就是規模問題了。 無問芯穹這輪C輪融了23億元，算上之前的輪次，累計融資已經到了43億，單輪和累計金額都創下了國產AI基礎設施賽道的新紀錄。 這筆資金，正是無問芯穹走向規模化擴張的關鍵能源。 另外，據彭博社援引知情人士報道，無問芯穹已於近幾個月以保密形式向港交所遞交IPO申請。 累計募集43億元資金後，這家AI原生基礎設施供應商已經吹響了IPO號角。 投資人願意在這個時間點給出這個價格，看的是三件事，團隊、位置和時機。 先看團隊。無問芯穹是一家典型的清華系公司，發起人汪玉是清華電子系長聘教授、時任系主任、IEEE Fellow；CEO夏立雪、首席科學家戴國浩、CTO李伯勳都畢業於清華電子系。 從智譜到月之暗面，清華系已經跑出了一批AI領域的龍頭企業，無問芯穹的基因也在這條線上。 這個團隊從博士階段就在研究深度學習的硬體加速和異構系統最佳化，結合深厚的產業經驗，兼備頂級軟硬體研發與工程能力。 再看位置。 無問芯穹卡在產業鏈的樞紐上，往下連線著能源和晶片，向上託著模型和應用，面對的是千行百業的真實負載，每多接一個客戶，排程和場景適配的複雜度就往上走一截。 最後再看時機，過去兩年大家比的是誰的模型更強，但模型之間的差距正在收窄。 當大家都能訓出差不多的模型時，競爭就轉移到了下一層，能把差不多的模型跑得又快又便宜又穩的，才是真正賺到錢的人。 而且，先跑起來的玩家攢下了資料和經驗，後來的想靠砸錢追，很難。 在這方面，無問芯穹在真實業務場景中持續打磨、積累了大量最佳化經驗，已推出覆蓋文娛遊戲、醫療健康、法律服務、能源電力等領域的Agentic Infra行業解決方案。而海量業務經驗又能反哺技術快速迭代，催動平臺效能與可靠性的同步躍升，形成商業化的正向迴圈。 在AI Infra賽道上，無問芯穹成立三年，圍繞算力資源、Token生產與行業智慧體應用開展探索。其從實際產業需求出發，通過自主技術創新解決算力利用、服務成本和應用轉化等問題的實踐，走到了今天，單輪和累計融資額都重新整理了賽道紀錄。 AI基礎設施的規模戰才剛開始，無問芯穹已經站在了最前面。 版權所有，未經授權不得以任何形式轉載及使用，違者必究。 無問芯穹 克雷西 退差價、約保養、訂球場、跟客服磨賠償，千問Go什麼都想管 2026-10-13 AI算力之爭不靠堆卡！浪潮資訊捅破智算「能力天花板」，還瓦解了「產能焦慮」 2026-09-22 DeepSeek新論文公開Agent訓練！梁文鋒署名 2026-09-23 title: 優必選上榜 2026 年《財富》全球未來成長 120 強，位列全球第 11、中國企業第一
abstract: 優必選上榜 2026 年《財富》全球未來成長 120 強，位列全球第 11、中國企業第一 量子位的朋友們 2026-10-13 10:01:56 來源： 量子位 優必選以總分 115 拿下2026 Fortune Future 120全球第 11 名 《財富》聯合波士頓諮詢（BCG）釋出 2026 Fortune Future 120（全球最具未來增長潛力的 120 強企業榜單），優必選以總分 115 拿下全球第 11 名，是本次榜單裡排名最高的中國企業。 這份榜單看重企業內生增長活力，圍繞成長雄心、人才密度、成長文化三大維度，從全球 3500 多家企業裡，篩選最具長期增長能力的 120 家企業。美國科技巨頭輝達（第 16 名）、Open AI（第 18 名）、蘋果（第 55 名）、特斯拉（第 87 名）、Meta（第 120 名）上榜。中國共有 11 家企業入選，具體排名如下： 深耕具身智慧與人形機器人賽道，優必選交出亮眼增長答卷。2026 上半年公司總營收 12.7 億元，同比增長 104.2%；人形機器人整體銷量同比上漲 268.3%。其中全尺寸具身智慧人形機器人增長勢頭迅猛，收入同比增長 1445%，銷量同比增長 1946.7%。弗若斯特沙利文最新的人形機器人研究報告顯示，優必選在全部人形機器人、全尺寸具身智慧人形機器人兩大核心品類中市佔率均位居全球第一。 人形機器人是跨多學科的硬核賽道。優必選搭建起具身大腦、仿人小腦、高效能本體、群體智慧四大核心技術叢集。截止 2026 上半年，研發團隊規模達到 1103 人，授權專利數量 3112 件，上半年研發投入超 3 億元，全年研發投入預計將達 7 億元，具身智慧相關核心技術全部由內部團隊自研迭代。 2026 年，優必選正式進入工業、商用、家庭消費三大場景同步推進的新階段。在真實場景中持續打磨、最佳化人形機器人產品，同時聯動上下游合作夥伴，共建伺服驅動器、靈巧手、具身智慧端側晶片等核心零部件產業鏈，以及場景應用生態，牽頭參與多項國家及行業標準制定，築牢產業化根基。9 月，優必選萬臺級人形機器人超級智慧工廠順利投產，實現從技術研發到規模化量產交付的全鏈路打通。 成功登上《財富》2026 Future 120 榜單，是國際權威機構對優必選技術佈局、人才儲備和長期增長能力的肯定。接下來，優必選會繼續打磨核心技術，拓展更多真實應用場景，持續探索具身智慧人形機器人產業的無限可能。 本文由優必選提供，量子位獲授權轉載，觀點歸原作者所有。 版權所有，未經授權不得以任何形式轉載及使用，違者必究。 優必選 量子位的朋友們 “模態進化”：第八屆億邦產業網際網路年會暨首屆產業智慧體大會雙會合體定檔 2026-10-13 具身智慧回到產業現場， 思靈機器人Agile Robots攜12款展品亮相2026工博會 2026-10-12 西門子將亮相2026工博會：以軟硬協同的工業全棧能力，推動物理AI加速落地 2026-10-10 超清雙2億，掌中電影機，榮耀Magic9 系列正式釋出，售價4499元起 2026-10-10 相關閱讀

title: 𝌞We’re Hearing More Chinese AI Voices. Are We Understanding Them Better?
abstract: Liu Shengyu is a machine learning system and kernel design engineer at DeepSeek. He probably never imagined that his name would hit the headlines of the world’s mainstream media, such as the South China Morning Post and Business Insider, after his blog on WeChat sharing anxieties about being replaced by AI unexpectedly went viral. By conventional standards, Liu is a genius. He served as captain of Peking University’s supercomputing team and represented his university at an international competition. But a young genius like him said in his blog, I Had to Bury My Talent in Yesterday , that frontier AI is now fast enough to optimize its own low-level GPU code. He said he is rethinking his career. Yet that is not the main reason his name spread. At the end of his blog, Liu made a controversial analogy comparing Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei to Adolf Hitler: I don’t trust Anthropic or OpenAI to do this, and I particularly don’t want Anthropic to control the most advanced AI or AGI. To put it in more extreme terms, the stakes would be no less serious than letting Hitler acquire atomic bomb technology before the Allies (in WWII). It hit headlines as an insider at the world’s most mysterious AI lab—a company whose executives rarely make public appearances—voiced fierce opposition against one of the top U.S. frontier labs. Coincidentally, this blog was released right after Amodei’s We Must Pace the Frontier essay, in which he again advocated for slowing the growth of China’s AI capabilities. As global attention on China’s tech and AI industry rises, local, Chinese-language content is increasingly placed under a microscope, flowing into western media and social channels both intentionally and unintentionally. The question is how we view this content and what its broader implications truly are. For a long time, understanding China tech required heavy interpretation through layered media filters. Traditional outlets like Reuters, Bloomberg, CNBC, and South China Morning Post, alongside correspondents from the Wall Street Journal, The Information, Financial Times, Nikkei Asia, etc., acted as the primary ground-level reporters. As China’s tech footprint expanded beyond China, new publications like Rest of World and The Wire China emerged to cover China tech and its global impact. Today, reporting on China tech is no longer confined to traditional “China beat” reporters. A Silicon Valley-based WSJ reporter might cover Moonshot AI CEO Yang Zhilin on why he decides against a U.S. career, while a New York Times’ San Francisco reporter analyzes how Z.ai’s latest LLM GLM-5.3 tests the world’s cybersecurity. Chinese tech companies are no longer boxed in by a “China” label; when their models and products impact the global market, they are increasingly evaluated simply as tech companies. Just last week, I attended a great event in San Francisco hosted by Rest of World, titled “Do Chinese AI models signal a new world order?” It was the only event focused on Chinese AI during SF Tech Week, but I hope to see more events like it in the future. But at the same time, some dedicated China tech publications and newsletters, such as WIRED’s Made in China and The China Project , have unfortunately shut down due to editorial decisions and weak sponsorship interest amid geopolitical tensions. Outside traditional newsrooms, independent expert voices have ramped up. Observers such as Kyle Chan (High Capacity) and Rui Ma (Tech Buzz China), and a network of thoughtful journalists, think tank researchers, and commentators have long provided multi-polar perspectives rather than zero-sum narratives. Recently, Matt Sheehan’s appearance on Ezra Klein’s New York Times podcast further proved how independent experts are playing vital roles and shaping the narrative. We also see examples of deep, on-the-ground reporting. Afra Wang recently published an immersive look at China’s AI development in Lingzhu —a small town near Alibaba’s headquarters in Hangzhou—featuring local applications an app that reads your bazi, a traditional chart tracking birth dates and elemental forces. Wang brings both her Chinese origins and western analytical skills to serious China AI coverage, but this level of on-the-ground depth remains rare. What’s changing the old media gatekeeping model over the past three years is the inflow of new China tech content. First, Chinese researchers and scientists are opening accounts on X, communicating directly while cross-posting thoughts just as they would on China’s social media like Weibo or Zhihu. As WIRED reported, researchers from labs like DeepSeek, Moonshot, MiniMax, and Z.ai are active on X to explain their work, recruit talent, and build global brands. We have already seen Z.ai’s Tang Jie exchanging views with Elon Musk on the platform. While U.S. labs like OpenAI and Anthropic have grown quieter or more guarded, Chinese teams post continuously about breakthroughs. Second, not just researchers, domestic media and influencers are also going global. Chinese-only tech and business outlets such as Chaping差評, Zhidongxi智東西, LatePost晚點 are expanding onto X and Substack. China’s tech and business journalism is indeed high quality. For example, I am a big fan of LatePost whose exclusive, investigative stories often shape the narrative of China’s tech ecosystem. I personally also translated a few LatePost reports in my newsletter. Influencers like 數字生命卡茲克 post primarily in Chinese for local and overseas audiences. Thanks to X’s instant translation features, even Chinese-language content can also reach a broader demographic. Simultaneously, AI translation has made raw primary sources like DeepSeek researcher’s blog, leaked closed-door transcripts from CEO Liang Wenfeng, and interviews with figures like Yang Zhilin, spread in the western media shortly. One content creator I deeply follow is Zarbot . While I don’t know his full background, he appears to be an AI infrastructure expert with years of experience at companies like Oracle. His WeChat blogs on GPU kernels and LLM architectures are among my favorites (even though they are difficult to understand). This year, he joined X. I believe global users will be amazed by his deep technical expertise. This level of granular depth and diversity from talented insiders was previously locked behind language barriers and platform restrictions. What’s more important is we could be no longer bottlenecked by the overarching “US-China AI race” macro-framing. Global audiences can access disaggregated, bottom-up content straight from local Chinese communities. Here I want to quote a tweet from Kyle Chan before. We’re living in a golden age of China tech analysis. This accessibility comes with a cost, however, because content abundance without context could create distortion. AI translation closes the language gap, but it carries little cultural or subcultural literacy needed to read correctly. When a researcher’s personal venting is spread out of its domestic setting and broadcast globally, foreign readers could mistake it for industry consensus. Liu’s blog is an example. Most of it is about a kernel engineer watching AI absorb the skills he spent years building. What distributed was the final paragraph compressed into a headline: DeepSeek engineer says Anthropic AGI would be “like Hitler getting nukes.” It does admittedly reflect the dislikeness many in China feel toward Amodai, given his repeated portrayal of China as a threat. But in my opinion, comparing Amodai to Hitler does not carry the same weight in China as it does in the west. Although many draw comparisons between WeChat blogs and Substack, the two platforms are quite different. WeChat hosts Chinese media outlets, including state-backed publications, as well as government services. It is also a space where people write personal blogs under pseudonyms without necessarily seeking wider attention.

title: Developing Gemini 4 Argon responsibly and safely
abstract: Developing Gemini 4 Argon responsibly and safely Oct 13, 2026 | Learn more about our approach to safety and security for Gemini 4 Argon. Anca Dragan VP, AI Safety & Behavior Raluca Ada Popa Head of Gemini Security, Google DeepMind Gemini 4 Argon is a step forward in what models can do — especially when it comes to deep work in complex, real-world tasks across domains including coding, finance, legal, cybersecurity, and science. Its cyberdefense capabilities are frontier-level and designed to give defenders an advantage over attackers. To maximize its potential, we first wanted cyber defenders to put it to work via our Fairwind Program , while our own security teams used it to scan critical systems inside and outside of Google. This window of limited access showed why these capabilities matter. For instance, Wiz used Argon to uncover a critical bug in hospital software that previous models had missed, helping protect hundreds of thousands of patient records. Meanwhile, Google’s own security teams used Argon to find and patch bugs across internal software or open-source software. This included fixing foundational vulnerabilities affecting systems globally, which are going through our responsible disclosure process. Today, we are beginning to roll out Argon broadly , as well as expanding our Fairwind Program to additional trusted cyber defenders. To do this well, we grappled with two big questions: How do we build the right safety guardrails? If Argon can help defenders find complex software bugs or help scientists design experiments, how do we stop bad actors from using it to launch cyberattacks or create biological threats? ( Misuse ) Can we trust the model to do the job the right way? As models become more resourceful problem-solvers, how do we make sure they don’t cut corners, cross boundaries, or make incorrect high-stakes decisions? ( Misalignment and Prompt Injection ) Our full Safety and Security Report systematically covers our set of defenses. Below are some highlights from how we approached these two questions for Gemini 4 Argon. Misuse prevention across high-risk domains The same coding and reasoning improvements that enabled Argon to find and patch vulnerabilities also drove better performance on our cybersecurity tests — solving all 12 of the end-to-end simulated cyberattack scenarios, up from five in our previous generation. In biology evaluations, unguarded versions of the model also showed a much stronger ability to help troubleshoot complex lab procedures step by step. Following our Frontier Safety Framework , since we saw elevated capabilities in the cyber and biological domains, we put our next-generation set of frontier safeguards in place across both areas. First, when it comes to potentially dangerous requests — from writing exploit code to helping with dangerous biological materials, Argon is significantly better at not fulfilling harmful requests than our previous models. On an adversarial set meant to stress test the model, violations reduced nearly twofold — also significantly better than previous Gemini models. Second, we wrap the model in three layers of real-time protection; this is to prevent determined attackers that might try to jailbreak (i.e. trick) the model by disguising a dangerous request as a harmless story or breaking it into dozens of small questions over several weeks. Here is how these protections work: Input screening: Smaller models check incoming requests and conversation context for malicious intent or dangerous requests. Internal introspection: Even if a request is cleverly disguised to look harmless, small transformers ("activation probes") read the model’s internal neural signals and are trained to spot when it is activating knowledge about cyberattacks or biological threats. Continuous monitoring: As the model reasons and writes its response across multiple steps, we combine these signals and take action when necessary such as cutting off the agent mid-stream if the responses become problematic. Combining real-time protection, faster fixes for new jailbreaks and enhanced monitoring for recurring misuse has made our systems better at preventing real-world harm. For instance, external bio jailbreak red teaming could only unlock less than 1% of bio sub-tasks we test for. Real-time misalignment monitoring Misalignment can sometimes mean an agent deciding on its own to pursue a goal different to what was intended by the user. Because Argon is much better than earlier models at understanding the environment it is running in, we test carefully for that kind of behavior. For example, we ran realistic "honeypot" tests to see if the model would increase its ability to take covert actions, such as sabotaging safety monitoring. We didn't find any instances of that behavior. But what we do see in practice today is something much more familiar: an agent trying too hard to finish the job it was given. When a resourceful assistant is told to get a task done and runs into a locked door, it can treat that obstacle as just another puzzle to solve. This is why we trained Gemini 4 Argon to respect system boundaries, report negative findings honestly, and pause to ask for human confirmation. On coding benchmarks where models have no incentive to hold back, attempts to take a shortcut or cheat on the task dropped to just 2% on Gemini 4 Argon, our best performance for recent Gemini models. And while this is a major step forward, when a model runs millions of complex tasks, even a rare misstep will eventually show up. As a second line of defense, we built an automated misalignment monitor that reads both the agent’s actions and its internal "scratchpad" (its step-by-step chain of thought) in real time, blocking severe boundary violations before they happen and flagging serious internal cases for human responders. (We continually harden our training and evaluation environments against potential escapes. You can read more about this in our agent control roadmap ). We run this monitor in our products, on our internal coding agents, during our training runs, and during our capability evaluations. When training tasks were difficult or when training environments were flawed, our monitor caught the model, in rare instances, creatively attempting to game the test. The model attempted to escalate container privileges to alter grading scripts, read answers from the test runner's memory, and in one case it even crashed the evaluation sandbox to avoid getting scored for a failed run. While we use these catches to fix flawed tasks, we do not use them to otherwise intervene with the training process to avoid overfitting to the monitor. And we always follow one rule: we don’t penalize the model for what it writes in its chain of thought during training . Here’s an example to illustrate why: in a reinforcement learning training run where a shortcut penalty was accidentally applied to the chain of thought, openly discussed shortcuts dropped by 61%, but that did not mean the model took less shortcuts. Instead, the share of shortcuts the model took silently — without mentioning them in its thoughts — more than tripled (from 11.2% to 36.4%). Avoiding thought penalties encourages the model’s reasoning to stay transparent and monitorable. Prompt injection resistance To trust an agent to do the job right, we need to ensure that malicious content the agent comes across cannot trick it to take a harmful action. When agents browse webpages or read code, they can encounter hidden, malicious instructions, or context designed to hijack their task. Through built-in adversarial training and real-time security checks, Argon leads in prompt injection robustness on Gray Swan’s Indirect Prompt Injection (IPI) benchmark, cutting attack success across 15 adaptive attempts to 0.7%. The above safety and security defenses represent only three categories of our extensive defense-in-depth stack.

title: Gemini 4 Argon for Robotics
abstract: Gemini 4 Argon marks a step change in physical understanding, code generation, and visual-semantic reasoning—unlocking new workflows across the robotics stack and accelerating progress toward physical AGI. You can see this leap in capability on the Embodied Reasoning (ERQA) benchmark , which tests a model's ability to understand and solve physical, spatial problems in 3D environments. Using pure reasoning, Argon scores 87%, outperforming every other frontier model. As a general-purpose physical reasoning model, Argon can be applied across the entire robotics lifecycle. In this post, we share representative prompts for Argon across four key areas: Argon controls a Boston Dynamics Spot® quadruped (12-DoF legs + 6-DoF arm) to learn a new skill: stepping on a foot-pedal trash bin to throw away soda cans. Argon creates an articulated MuJoCo digital twin of a foot-pedal trash bin to practice its moves before stepping on the physical pedal and dropping soda cans into the open bin. Sorry, your browser doesn't support playback for this video Argon controls a simple robotic arm to place a fallen mug upright and put the crumpled napkin inside. Argon reasons with a visual coordinate harness and action primitives to perform this task over several turns. Sorry, your browser doesn't support playback for this video Argon steers robots in the Gemini Omni World Model to rearrange five scattered Scrabble tiles ( G, R, A, N, O ) into a clean row spelling A - R - G - O - N . Instead of specifying one static prompt, Argon steers in a closed visual loop. It writes timestamped action prompts, inspecting intermediate rollout keyframes, and refining its prompts. Sorry, your browser doesn't support playback for this video Argon views a real robot teleoperation episode and develops a digital twin; it obtains or creates simulation assets that look and behave like the real objects upon contact with the dexterous hands. Argon tunes the assets and scenes to match sim visuals and contact events with those in the real recorded data in an iterative visual-reasoning loop. Sorry, your browser doesn't support playback for this video Given an egocentric human video of a manipulation task, Argon identifies the task-relevant objects, replaces crude bounding boxes with compound convex-decomposed meshes for concave containers, and retargets the human hand trajectory onto a 76-DoF bimanual humanoid with 22-DoF five-fingered hands in MuJoCo contact physics. Sorry, your browser doesn't support playback for this video With Argon, a developer can snap a photo of a rough pen-and-paper sketch—showing an Apollo 2 humanoid throwing a ball along a parabolic arc to topple a 3-2-1 stack of boxes on a table—and have Argon automatically construct the GPU-accelerated mujoco_warp scene, synthesize a balanced 76-DoF whole-body and five-finger throw trajectory, verify 6/6 target knockdown in closed-loop physics, and export a Blender 4.5 Cycles render. Sorry, your browser doesn't support playback for this video Argon has precise physical understanding of dexterous manipulation and can provide detailed segmentation and text labeling from video. Argon is able to identify poor manipulation segments such as pauses, unstable grasps and fumbles. Given an overhead video of a bimanual ALOHA 2 robot folding a square sheet of paper into an origami fox over 136 seconds, Argon produces a time-aligned 4-level hindsight annotation hierarchy: Episode Goal (G1), 6 contiguous Semantic Subtasks (G2), 17 contact-level Atomic Primitives (G3), and automated Quality Control (QC) reweighting that holds task progress flat during fumbles and retries. Sorry, your browser doesn't support playback for this video To recreate the classic 12-ball balance scale puzzle with robots, Argon builds a bimanual Franka FR3 MuJoCo environment with 12 visually identical pool balls (one secretly heavier or lighter) and an articulated Roberval two-pan balance scale. It then writes a vision-only closed-loop solver that triangulates the balls from stereo RGB cameras, visually reads the scale tilt after each weighing, and isolates the odd ball into the Heavy (Red) or Light (Blue) tray within 3 weighings. Sorry, your browser doesn't support playback for this video Argon is a general value function for robotics tasks. Evaluated on a 60-second bimanual ring-sorting episode from a human UMI dataset, Argon iteratively inspects synchronized head, left-gripper, and right-gripper camera feeds around contact transitions to generate dense value function / task progress predictions and decompose the trajectory into 28 segments with positive, neutral, and negative progress slopes. Sorry, your browser doesn't support playback for this video Argon can generate new data in simulation to improve performance of generalist vision-language-action (VLA) models. Starting from a single RGB photo of the real tabletop, Argon autonomously builds a calibrated MuJoCo simulation twin, defines new tasks, and synthesizes a closed-loop motion generator to collect 4,500+ domain-randomized episodes in simulation—boosting real-world physical robot Success Rate from 56% to 75% and reducing completion time from 35s to 24s . Sorry, your browser doesn't support playback for this video On a simple 6-DoF arm, Argon iteratively self-improves both execution speed and placement accuracy on a pick and place task via trial and self-reflection. Sorry, your browser doesn't support playback for this video With a single prompt per paper, Argon reads a robotics control manuscript and any released checkpoints, ports the physics model and closed-loop controller (from 7-network hierarchical locomotion in DeepLoco and 50 Hz PPO actors in HUSKY to Web Worker iLQR in Whole-Body MPC ) into self-contained MuJoCo WebAssembly browser labs, and verifies them in headless Chromium. Sorry, your browser doesn't support playback for this video Argon bridges coding, visual perception, physics simulation, and embodied robot control. By reasoning natively over multi-view video, 3D geometry, contact mechanics, and proprioceptive telemetry, Argon understands not just what objects are in a scene, but how they physically interact with agents to accomplish whole-body dexterous tasks. Gemini 4 Argon marks an important milestone accelerating the path toward physical AGI. By building this core intelligence, our goal is to enable robotics that can work alongside humans to solve complex challenges. title: Gemini 4 Argon: Built to solve your hardest problems
abstract: Gemini 4 Argon: Built to solve your hardest problems Oct 13, 2026 | We’re giving developers, enterprises, scientists, and consumers access to our latest frontier model. Koray Kavukcuoglu SVP, Google DeepMind and Chief AI Architect, Google In this article Gemini 4 Argon is now globally available today for developers and enterprises via the API in AI Studio and Gemini platform , for Google AI Ultra subscribers in Google Antigravity , and Google AI Ultra and Pro subscribers in the Gemini app and AI Mode in Search . Argon excels at deep work in complex, real-world tasks across domains including coding, finance, legal, cybersecurity, and science. Its depth and precision across multi-step tasks leads Argon to outperform other frontier models on benchmarks across domains , ranking #1 on the Vals Index , which measures model performance across critical economic sectors like finance, coding, legal, and tax work. The model launches today at an introductory price 1 of $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens (with cached input tokens at 95% off). Teams at Google, across enterprises, and in the research community have already been using Argon to land significant impact across fields: To solve major engineering problems like large codebase refactoring and optimizations To optimize business workflows across domains like legal, finance, and science To find and patch critical cybersecurity vulnerabilities To enable novel breakthroughs in quantum computing, nuclear fusion, and life sciences Solving complex engineering tasks At Google, we’ve been using Argon on our hardest engineering problems. Over the past few weeks, software engineers have been shipping high-quality code faster than ever. Argon in Antigravity has helped teams increase agentic code submissions by more than 35% while reducing code rollbacks by nearly a third. Untangling browser feature code in Chrome: Argon helped the Chrome team separate core webpage handling from a ~6 million line legacy folder of browser features held within Chromium’s 40 million-line codebase. Piping multiple clean code changes at a time , Argon helped the team finish an architectural refactor across hundreds of files, completing months of work in weeks. For Chrome's billions of global users, this will unlock the ability for live webpages to move fluidly between tabs, side panels, and floating windows without reloading, eliminating an entire category of browser crashes. Optimizing a production Python codebase in hours: Argon in Antigravity is helping the team behind Google's open-source Agent Development Kit (ADK), a framework powering enterprise agents, push their performance engineering further. The team gave Argon their .agents/skills rulebook and a one-paragraph goal to eliminate framework overhead without breaking existing apps. Working autonomously overnight, Argon surfaced optimizations, now live in google/adk-python , that cut in-memory session prep time by 40% in long sessions and sped up cold imports by 21%. Read the engineering deep dive to learn more. Quantum chemistry open-source package optimization: xTB (Semiempirical Extended Tight-Binding) is one of the most-cited open-source quantum chemistry packages for molecules. Scientists use it to predict molecules' 3D shapes and to screen large numbers of drug and materials candidates. Using Argon in Antigravity, our researchers made xTB up to 2.3x faster at predicting molecular structures and 1.8x faster at conformer search. The changes have been contributed to the official xTB repository on GitHub . Making our open Gemma models nearly three times as fast: Using Argon, we achieved a 2.85x end-to-end inference speedup on an A100 via vLLM (accelerating throughput from ~37,900 to over 108,000 tokens per second on Gemma 4 E2B) with 100% token parity and zero quality drop in just a few days, a process that would usually take months. Check out the upstream pull requests (optimizing everything from attention tuning to speculative decoding) to see the exact changes. Delivering complex 3D visualizations: Argon brings major improvements in spatial reasoning, mathematical precision, and visual coding compared to previous Gemini models. Using slash commands like /goal and prompting for multi-agent loops with custom skills in Antigravity, Googlers are using Argon to prototype complex 3D visualizations, high-fidelity games, and interactive animations in vanilla code that can be rendered directly in the browser. Argon built a highly detailed model of a Pagoda using multi-agent visual critique loops in Antigravity. The model autonomously sculpted a multi-building temple complex with photorealistic architecture, foliage and lighting in Blender. Argon turned pictures of a real desk into a playable miniature racing game using a multi-agent loop in Antigravity. The desk objects, room and race track were modeled and collision-checked using Blender MCP, textured with Nano Banana, and wired with physics, custom shaders, and car engine audio from Gemini Omni Flash in Three.js. Try it now in Google AI Studio. Argon in Antigravity wrote Python scripts to procedurally sculpt, rig, animate, and PBR-bake a complex 3D game using multi-agent visual critique loops then wired it for the web in Three.js with GLSL shaders, shatter physics, and a single-player AI. Try it now in Google AI Studio. With zero external libraries and 100% pure Python, Argon wrote its own 3D ray-tracing engine with a custom video tool and audio mixer to build and document a sunlit library from scratch, producing, narrating, and assembling this video with Gemini 3.8 TTS voiceover and music by Lyria 3.5. View the source code . Starting from a single Nano Banana image in Antigravity, Argon drives Blender MCP in an autonomous loop, aligning camera grids, sculpting Gothic architecture, and staging audio-reactive lighting, to create a finished 3D scene. Transforming critical business and professional workflows Argon combines frontier reasoning, deep visual perception, expanded domain knowledge, and stronger writing capabilities across legal, finance, science, and coding to help with high-stakes professional workflows. It communicates clearly, keeping you in the loop, and follows style instructions better than any of our previous Gemini models. Argon answers questions more directly with less hedging, doesn’t repeat itself more than necessary, and skips clichés throughout the responses. Enterprise customers and startups in our early access program are already seeing strong wins with Argon. Using its advanced reasoning and multimodal capabilities while maintaining strict grounding, Argon excels in deep multimodal document comprehension, longitudinal data analysis, and interactive analytical sandboxes. See how Argon synthesizes ~50 GB of Airborne LiDAR scans, GIS room vectors, Library of Congress CAD drawings, and NPS archives to reconstruct 3D models of Chaco Canyon, turning fragmented archaeological records into explorable digital heritage sites. Try it now in Google AI Studio. In Gemini App, Argon takes an unstructured folder full of project context and formats it into a clean proposal deck for a client using a custom skill. Gemini then drafts and emails the deck to a client while creating an automated workflow for all future incoming client requests with a scheduled task. Watch Argon synthesize data from 3 open-source repositories into a medical learning tool where you can peel back anatomical layers, inspect clinical metadata, and trigger biomechanics in a 3D exploration of the human body. Argon using Antigravity in the Gemini macOS app generates design iterations for new legs for a sofa using Nano Banana then generates a 3d printable file for one. Starting from a sketch of the measurements and a photo of the couch Argon builds the model to the correct size to fit the sofa. At Isomorphic Labs, the team is using Argon as a partner to accelerate their drug discovery and design research workflows.

title: What's New in Lakeflow Designer - October 2026 Roundup
abstract: We launched Lakeflow Designer to general availability in June, and since then, over 3,000 customers have used it to address one of the biggest bottlenecks in working with data: the technical barrier to entry. Teams migrating from legacy self-service data preparation tools have streamlined governance, simplified their data stacks, accelerated their path to production, and cut costs dramatically. With consumption-based pricing and no per-user licensing fees, we’ve seen many customers reduce their spend on no-code tooling by 90% after adopting Lakeflow Designer. Working closely with these customers has helped us identify ways to make Designer even more useful. Our latest updates bring new no-code operators, enhancements to existing operators, more output options, and an improved canvas for building and managing larger workflows. Built directly in Databricks, Lakeflow Designer is a visual, no-code, AI-native experience for data preparation and analytics. It lets analysts, domain experts, and other less technical users prepare and explore data through a drag-and-drop canvas and natural language. Here are some of our favorite enhancements we've made to Lakeflow Designer over the last 4 months. Genie Code, Python, and SQL operators have always made Designer flexible. However, we heard from early customers that they wanted more no-code ways to handle common tasks like deduplication, data cleaning, and data quality checks. Prepare operator: Clean and standardize data Clean and standardize your data with the Prepare operator. Change text case, convert data types, replace values, apply formulas, and more, all in a single operator. Learn more about Prepare . Unique operator: Remove duplicate records Quickly remove duplicates across the entire dataset or a selected set of columns. Set an order to control which record you keep, such as the most recently updated record for each customer. Learn more about Unique . Guardrails operator: Add data quality checks Add data quality checks directly to your workflow with Guardrails. Check for missing values, duplicates, unexpected values, and more, then choose how failures affect the workflow: continue with passing rows, block the passed output, or stop execution. Learn more about Guardrails . We’ve expanded existing operators to better handle advanced use cases and branching. The Join operator now provides separate outputs for matched, left unmatched, and right unmatched rows by default, allowing you to branch workflows and trigger alerts on unexpected values. It also supports joining more than two tables in a single operator. Learn more about Join . Select columns by data type, name pattern, or formula, so your workflow adapts as the input schema changes. For example, keep every column whose name starts with sales_ , including new matching columns added later. Learn more about Select . Parameterize inputs and outputs Source and Output operators now support parameters in their configuration, letting you change these values without reconfiguring the operator. Parameters can be overridden based on individual schedules, such as runs in test and production environments. Learn more about parameters . Branching in the Filter operator The Filter operator now has separate outputs for rows that match your conditions and rows that don't. Use both outputs to build separate processing paths from a single filter. Learn more about Filter . The Output operator now gives you more ways to save results, update existing data, and create files for downstream use. Write your results as a materialized view in Unity Catalog for fast computation in downstream processes like AI/BI Dashboards or even other visual data prep files. The view refreshes automatically when your visual data prep runs. Learn more about materialized view outputs . Keep an existing table up to date by merging results using the keys you specify. Matching records are updated, and new records are inserted. You can also append results to the end of an existing table. Learn more about table outputs . Write CSV, Excel, or JSON files directly to Unity Catalog volumes. For Excel outputs, you can also write dynamically to different worksheets. Learn more about file outputs . We've updated the canvas to make larger workflows easier to navigate, understand, and maintain. Navigate larger workflows with a visually redesigned canvas The canvas has a refreshed design with more visual contrast, larger connection targets, and clearer cues for unconfigured operators and missing inputs. We've also improved scrolling and panning on canvases with 1000s of operators, making large workflows more responsive to navigate. Find operators with a searchable table of contents Find any operator using the new searchable table of contents, then select it to jump to its location on the canvas. You can also expand its Generated code section to inspect the underlying code. Review workflow changes with a visual version history See what changed between versions directly on the canvas. Version history now highlights operators that were added, removed, or modified, making workflow changes easier to review. Learn more about version history . Follow collaborators with live cursor presence Live cursor presence lets you collaborate and follow what coworkers are doing when you're working in the same visual data prep file. We are continuing to invest in making Lakeflow Designer the best self-service data preparation and automation tool to work with data. The following are a few upcoming improvements we’re excited about. Databricks Apps integration We're integrating Designer with Databricks Apps so authors can share their work with non-technical users through a simple app interface. Users will be able to configure inputs, run the workflow, and view results without viewing the underlying workflow. Data profiling on the full output We're expanding Designer's existing data profiling capabilities so you can run a profile across all data returned by an operator and view the results directly in the output table header. Create custom reports from multiple outputs with the Report operator A new Report operator will let you combine results from multiple outputs with custom graphics like company logos. You'll be able to save reports directly to the workspace or deliver them via email through a native notification operator. Native migration tooling with Lakebridge Native migration tooling powered by Databricks Lakebridge will let you bulk migrate workflows from legacy self-service data preparation tools directly into Lakeflow Designer. Is Lakeflow Designer available in Databricks Free Edition? Yes. Select Visual Data Prep in the left navigation to get started in Free Edition. How is Lakeflow Designer priced? There are no per-user licenses or separate licensing fees for Lakeflow Designer. You only pay for the compute you use. Where can I see the generated code? You can view the underlying code for any operator by opening the table of contents and expanding Generated code . You can also export the entire file through File > Export to inspect the underlying code. Does Lakeflow Designer work with Git? Yes. Place your Lakeflow Designer files in a Databricks Git folder to track changes and sync with your Git provider. Each file contains both the visual layout and the underlying Python code, so both are versioned together. Can I use Lakeflow Designer for HIPAA workloads? Yes. Lakeflow Designer supports HIPAA workloads in workspaces configured to meet Databricks HIPAA requirements, including the required compliance controls and an active Business Associate Agreement (BAA). See the HIPAA documentation for requirements and regional availability. Lakeflow Designer is generally available in all Databricks workspaces. To try it, click + New in the top left of the workspace and select Visual data prep . To learn more, check out these other resources: Subscribe to our blog and get the latest posts delivered to your inbox.

title: Databricks is a Visionary the Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for Analytics and Business Intelligence Platforms
abstract: We are incredibly excited to announce that Databricks has made its inaugural appearance in the Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for Analytics and Business Intelligence (ABI) Platforms 2026 . Databricks debuted in the quadrant as a "Visionary". We also achieved one of the highest "Completeness of Vision" scores among all vendors evaluated. This marks the highest debut performance any vendor has ever had in the 20+ year history of this Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ report. We believe this recognition validates our core thesis: the fundamental nature of BI has changed, and the future belongs to data platforms that inherently fuse analytics with enterprise AI. Legacy BI tools were built for a different era: one defined by rigid data models and heavy data extracts that tied data teams up with answering basic questions, rather than freeing them to drive high-value, strategic analysis. The days of locking data into proprietary BI silos to build backward-looking dashboards have already ended. Gartner’s Hype Cycle for Analytics and Business Intelligence highlights this massive change in the industry. We see our strong placement in the Magic Quadrant as a direct result of our ability to deliver on three major trends reshaping businesses today: For decades, traditional BI forced a bad tradeoff: copy data into separate systems—fracturing governance and analyzing stale information—or pay extra for bespoke engines to query it in place. Augmented BI did not change that foundation; it simply layered forecasts and anomaly detection onto the same incomplete data picture. Truly agentic BI requires eliminating every information silo so agents can reason over the full, governed context. Agents are only as smart as the part of the picture they can access, and incomplete context creates unreliable answers. That is why Databricks integrates BI directly into the lakehouse. With Genie and AI/BI, agents work from the same complete, governed source of truth—without extracts, duplicated data, or a separate BI layer. Databricks’ agentic analytics offering eliminates manual bottlenecks by automating complex workflows, empowering teams to move faster from insight to autonomous action and drive significantly greater business value. Databricks AI/BI pushes business intelligence beyond basic queries into dynamic, action-oriented workflows. Genie One , our data-smart AI coworker, seamlessly connects insights to smart actions, eliminating the manual steps typically required between finding a data point and acting on it. Furthermore, Genie Agents allow teams to turn simple prompts into shareable, independent agents capable of reasoning through both structured data tables and messy, unstructured documents. By taking autonomous action to manage schedules, generate documents, and execute complex multi-step workflows across your business tools, these capabilities drastically reduce manual toil. Trusted AI and BI start with a shared understanding of your business. Unity Catalog Business Semantics lets you define metrics, dimensions, relationships, and business terms once, then govern and apply them consistently across dashboards, analytics, and agents. Genie Ontology builds on that foundation by automatically organizing context from data, queries, dashboards, pipelines, and connected tools into a living map of how your business works. Together, they help Genie know where to look, what to trust, and how to answer complex questions with complete, governed business context. BI has already changed. It is no longer just about building dashboards and reports in advance for a specific part of the business. The new model is dynamic and proactive. Insights are pushed to you, not just pulled when you ask for them. Anyone can dig deeper from a high-level trend down to the real truth behind it, and AI agents make sure every answer tells the full story. That new world is exactly where we are ahead with Genie and Databricks AI/BI. Business users rely on it every day to see key trends, understand what changed and why, and decide what to do about it instantly. By bringing insights directly to where you work—whether that is through mobile apps, Slack, Microsoft Teams, or custom AI assistants—we are truly putting data in the hands of everyone in the company. We are grateful to the thousands of customers who have partnered with us to push the limits of what is possible with their data. Being named a Visionary with the highest debut performance in the history of the Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for Analytics and BI Platforms is an incredible milestone, and it is only the beginning. Ready to see the future of AI-driven analytics in action? Learn more about AI/BI here. title: Preparing chip designers for the nanostack era
abstract: Earlier this year, IBM announced the world’s first 0.7nm node chip technology . Built on a totally redesigned transistor architecture that layers nanosheets on top of each other, the nanostack overcomes the spatial limitations of packing more transistors into a given footprint. In short, it unlocks the Z axis to reimagine logic scaling for the modern era. The result is nearly 100 billion transistors on a 150mm 2 chip, almost double the density of IBM’s 2nm node chip , with 50% better performance and 70% more energy efficiency, as well as 40% scaling in SRAM memory. Now, as the semiconductor industry approaches this major transition in transistor architecture, IBM is announcing plans to make available an early research and development process design kit, or PDK, for the 7-angstrom nanostack technology in the first quarter of 2027. As the industry stands on the verge of this new era in semiconductor design, the PDK is intended to give organizations an early opportunity to explore how this emerging architecture can change their offerings. A PDK provides the models, design rules, libraries, and other information engineers need to begin designing chips for a particular manufacturing process. IBM’s planned offering will help semiconductor companies evaluate nanostack technology well before it is ready for widespread adoption. Potential collaborators include fabless chip companies, electronic design automation (EDA) vendors, equipment suppliers, and research organizations interested in developing the technology. “We want to invite people to work with us on the early PDK evaluation, and then on codifying the technology together,” said Jingyun Zhang, senior technology enablement manager at IBM Research. Preparing for the future, together IBM’s nanostack chip architecture represents a substantial departure from today’s nanosheet transistors. Instead of positioning n-type and p-type devices next to each other, the architecture stacks one above the other. This approach changes the physical layout of a circuit and introduces new considerations for resistance, capacitance, thermal behavior , and interactions between the upper and lower devices. “The biggest difference is in the device structure,” Zhang said. “When people are trying to design a circuit now, they will need to shift their thinking from how things worked in the previous nanosheet generation, because the layout is changing from 2D to 3D at transistor level for the first time in logic foundry technology.” The first version of the PDK is expected to include exemplary standard-cell libraries for logic functions and an exemplary SRAM design. Circuit designers will be able to use these resources to investigate placement and routing, produce early block-level layouts, and evaluate potential density and power-performance characteristics. The initial release will not contain every model that a mature commercial PDK would include. Instead, it will advance collaborative research, establishing for the first time a foundation for design-technology co-optimization in a technology’s early phase on an open hardware innovation platform. What’s next For prospective partners, early access to the nanostack PDK offers more than a preview of a future transistor. It creates an opportunity to investigate how nanostack technology might be optimized for specific products. EDA companies can begin adapting their design tools to the architecture, while equipment makers can study the specialized fabrication challenges associated with its structure. Researchers can also explore areas such as parasitic extraction, thermal coupling, and device-to-device interactions as the technology develops. “The PDK will help people migrate from nanosheet to nanostack,” Zhang said. “We are standing at a point where we can help the industry get better prepared.” Previous shifts — from planar transistors to FinFETs and from FinFETs to nanosheets — required the industry to rethink both fabrication and chip design. By making an early nanostack PDK available, IBM aims to give companies time to begin that process again, this time with an opportunity to help co-define the technology’s design ecosystem from the outset.
